title: Runbook Mesh: step autotagger & replayable snippet registry
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Our current runbook-as-tasks backlog has many one-off snippets and patch scripts stuffed into long playbooks. When oncall engineers search for remediation steps they often find duplicated variants and non-idempotent shell fragments. Goal: build a small runway to (1) automatically classify and tag individual runbook steps (detects side-effecting ops, DB writes, network calls, and required perms), (2) extract and store canonical, templatized snippets into a replayable registry with metadata (inputs, outputs, idempotency hints, required scopes), and (3) expose a light query API and UI component so support can discover and replay safe steplets during incidents.

Scope: MVP covers Linux/YAML step formats used in our runbook corpus, basic static heuristics + lightweight runtime checks for idempotency, registry storage with versioning and provenance, and a small console surface to search and preview steplets. This ticket covers backend indexing, autotagger ruleset, snippet normalization, and registry write/read endpoints. Console integration tracked separately.

Acceptance criteria:
- Autonomous indexer runs on nightly job and ingests new runbook commits, producing tagged steplets with provenance links to origin runbook and PR.
- Snippets stored in registry include: canonicalized command/template, declared inputs, estimated side-effects, idempotency_hint (one of: guaranteed, likely, non-idempotent, unknown), and a canonical test snippet that can be run in sandbox.
- Query API supports filters: label, idempotency_hint, required_scope, author, last_run, and fuzzy text. Latency for index lookup < 150ms p95 for normal queries.
- Oncall engineers can replay a snippet in read-only sandbox (dry-run) or request an approver flow for privileged replay. Audit log entries created for every replay request.
- End-to-end tests and a small QA playbook to validate common remediation paths.
updates: 2025-11-18: Spike completed. Ran corpus analysis across ~2.3k runbooks, identified ~7.1k candidate steps. Initial heuristics for idempotency (file writes, kubectl apply, DB migrations) recall ~78% on sample set.
2025-11-25: Chose storage model: immutable steplet objects with lightweight manifest and provenance pointer to runbook commit. Implemented prototype schema in Dynamo table 'runbook-steplets-v1'.

2025-11-30: Built first autotagger pass using a rules engine (yaml + regex + small AST walker). False-positive rate high for custom scripts; planning to add runtime dry-run checks for commands that mutate external state.
2025-12-02: API scaffolding merged (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/492). Added start of list endpoint and basic filters. Need perf tuning for p95 latency under load.
2025-12-03: Cross-team review with SEC and SRE scheduled. Action items: add KMS-backed audit token for replay requests and document safe-replay RBAC matrix.
comments: Ravi Singh (assignee) - 2025-11-19: Noting we should leverage existing KV cache layer for the registry read path to hit the p95 goal. Will prototype a small LRU with 10k keys.
Yvonne Park (PM) - 2025-11-21: UX ask: add a quick 'why-tagged' tooltip that explains which heuristic fired for a steplet so support can trust suggestions.

Jonas Becker (SRE) - 2025-11-26: Concern: automated replay could enable accidental escalations. Recommend defaulting to dry-run for any step with 'likely' or 'unknown' idempotency_hint and routing privileged runs through an approver workflow.
